I fixed two bugs in the source, and `node --test` now passes all 9 tests. The tests themselves are unchanged.

**1. `src/bill.js`: off-by-one in `splitBill`** (caused 3 of the 4 failures)
The function gave an extra cent to people `0` through `leftover` using `i <= leftover`. That's one person too many: `splitBill(1000, 3)` returned `[334, 334, 333]`, which adds up to 1001. Even splits were wrong too, because with a leftover of 0, person 0 still got an extra cent (`[301, 300, 300]`). I changed the condition to `i < leftover`.

**2. `src/duration.js`: `parseDuration` accepted input with trailing text**
It used `matchAll` to pick out `\d+[hms]` pieces and only threw an error if there were none. So `"10m and change"` returned 600 instead of being rejected, and something like `"3d1h"` would have quietly returned 3600. It now checks the whole string first with `/^(?:\d+[hms])+$/` and throws a `SyntaxError` if anything else is in it. The existing parsing logic is unchanged.

The diff is one line in each file. Since the change was this small, I made it myself and didn't hand it off or ask for a separate review.
